blocks.prompt: 4 A cyclist travelled 48 km at a uniform speed. If he had travelled 2 km/hour slower, he would have taken 2 hours more to perform the journey. How long did he take to cover 48 km?
blocks.explanation:
A speed-time word problem: time \(=\) distance \(\div\) speed.
We must find the time taken for 48 km.
Plan: let the speed be \(v\) km/h, write both times, use "2 hours more" to form the equation, solve, then find the time.
steps:
Given: distance 48 km; at a speed 2 km/h less the journey takes 2 hours more.
To find: the time taken.
Method: Time \(= \frac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}}\). Write the two times; the slower time minus the usual time is 2. Solve for the speed first, then find the time.

Choose the unknown and write both times
\[\text{Let speed} = v \text{ km/h}\]
\[\text{time} = \dfrac{48}{v}\]
\[\text{slower time} = \dfrac{48}{v - 2}\]
Why: At the slower speed \(v - 2\) the same 48 km takes longer.

Form the equation
\[\dfrac{48}{v - 2} - \dfrac{48}{v} = 2\]
Why: "2 hours more" means the slower time minus the usual time is 2.

Clear the fractions
\[48v - 48(v - 2) = 2v(v - 2)\]
\[96 = 2v^2 - 4v\]
Why: Multiply every term by the LCD \(v(v - 2)\); \(48v - 48v\) cancels, leaving \(96\).

Standard form and factorize
\[v^2 - 2v - 48 = 0\]
\[(v - 8)(v + 6) = 0\]
\[v = 8 \text{ or } v = -6\]
Why: Divide by 2. \(-8 \times 6 = -48\) and \(-8 + 6 = -2\). Speed cannot be negative, so \(v = 8\) km/h.

Find the time
\[\text{time} = \dfrac{48}{8} = 6 \text{ hours}\]
Why: The question asks for the time, not the speed.

Check
\[\dfrac{48}{6} = 8 \text{ hours at } 6 \text{ km/h}\]
\[8 - 6 = 2 \;\checkmark\]
Why: At 2 km/h slower (6 km/h) the journey takes exactly 2 hours more.
blocks.final_answer: He took 6 hours (his speed was 8 km/h).
